identity.description:
Show the orchestrator's board in a pane, from one board --json source

## Summary

An orchestrator session can now show its board in a pane that stays current by itself. The new `/orch-board <name>` command opens the pane: plan usage first, then what needs the principal, then each group of items in merge order, then the single items. A row number and Enter brings that implementer's tab to the front, and a new item for the principal shows a toast. The board's content now has one source, `crew-orch.py board --json`, and both the text board and the pane draw from it, so the two cannot show different values.

Closes #155

**Ticket:** [#155 — crew:orchestrator: the board pane](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/155)
**Type:** New feature

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md` "The board" owns the board, its JSON shape, its version rule and `CREW_ORCH_NOW`.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md` owns `launcher.py focus <handle>`, which the pane runs.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/usage.md` owns `crew-usage.py show --json`, which the Plan block reads.
- `docs/design.md` §15.TBD records the decisions. Issue #150 holds the agreed layout.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/crew-orch.py`: `board --json` prints the board as one object (`board_data`); the text `board` draws from that object (`render_text`); a single item's row shows its own ticket; `CREW_ORCH_NOW` pins the time that `board` reads, for tests.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh`: checks the JSON shape and values, no write, one place per derived value, the text output against `origin/main` on a day-old record, the single item ticket, and the committed fixtures against a fresh run.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md`: "The board" documents the JSON fields, the version and compatibility rule, the single item ticket and `CREW_ORCH_NOW`.
- `hooks/orch-board.tsx`: the board pane mod. `/orch-board [<name>]` (else `$CREW_ORCH`) opens the pane; it runs `board --json` every 5 s while open, draws it, toasts new Needs-you ids, and runs `launcher.py focus` for a typed row number. It computes no board value and writes no file.
- `types/index.d.ts`: the board JSON types and the mod's `$.state` contract.
- `tests/orch-board.test.tsx`, `tests/fixtures/board-json.ts`, `tests/fixtures/board-text.ts`: 22 mod tests with a stub board command and a stub launcher; the fixtures that `test-crew-orch.sh` keeps current.
- `hooks/hooks.json`: `modules` names the mod beside the existing hooks.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: `types` names the types file. `version` in both manifests is the placeholder `0.1.TBD`, for the orchestrator to set.
- `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/design.md`: the Layout rows and Build state, the `/orch-board` command, and finding §15.TBD.

### Constraints that applied

- One definition of the board: every value is made in `board_data`; the text view and the pane only draw. A test greps for each derived value in one place.
- The text `board` output is byte for byte as on main, except the single item ticket the principal asked for.
- The pane reads no record file and writes no file; its kept state is `$.state`.
- No test starts `claude` with the user's plugins: `claude plugin test` and `claude plugin validate` ran with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a new empty directory. No test opens a tab.
- `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md` is not created (issue #154). The version and the §15 number are placeholders.

### How this was verified

- `bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh`: "all checks passed". At the red commit f85fc30 it failed with "unknown option --json".
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) claude plugin test .`: 22 pass, 0 fail, including the test that renders the JSON fixture at 200 columns and finds the same sections, rows and cells as the text fixture.
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) claude plugin validate .`: passed; its three warnings (marketplace description, root CLAUDE.md, icon) were on main before.
- The project lead read the whole diff of `crew-orch.py` and the mod against the spec.

### Known gaps

- No session has opened the pane yet. The key, the toast and the narrow layout ran only in the test kit.
- The test kit cannot raise a pane close, so the stop of the timer on close is tested through the open-pane list.
- `CLAUDE.md` is 280 lines, above the 200-line target; it was 270 before this change.

# Spec: the board pane (jerridan/crew#155)

Part of #150. Repo: `/Users/jerridan/src/crew/.claude/worktrees/orch-board`.
Layout source: issue #150, "The agreed board layout". Outcome list: issue #155.

Terms. The **text view** is the output of `crew-orch.py board`. The **JSON view** is the output of `crew-orch.py board --json`. The **mod** is a Claude Code hooks module of this plugin. The **pane** is what the mod draws. The **board data** is the JSON view.

## Requirements

Each requirement has one acceptance criterion (AC). A command or a checklist line can fail each AC.

### The board data

**R1. `board --json` prints the board as one JSON object.**
`board --json` prints one JSON object on stdout, and nothing else, then exits 0. The object is the one definition of the board content: the section order, the group order, the row order, the five marks, the status word, the row text, every age, the Needs-you list, the Done count, the footer legend and the Plan figures. Each value that the text view prints today is in the object, formatted as the text view shows it (for example the age `12m`, the status word and the marks string `●●●●◐`). The object also holds what a pane needs and the text view does not print: the PR URL, the item id and `n`, the ticket id and URL, and the `launch.tab` handle of the item (or `null`). The command reads the record alone, as `board` does, and never writes it. The strings in the object follow the same cleaning as the text view. The object holds no OSC 8 sequence.
AC: For one seeded record, `board --json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.load(sys.stdin)'` exits 0. A listing of the record files before and after the command is the same, and the bytes of every file are the same. A check of each field in "The board JSON" below finds the field, with the type that the table gives.

**R2. The text view draws from the JSON view data.**
Plain `board` and `board --urls` draw their text from the same data that `--json` prints. No derived value is computed in two places in `crew-orch.py`. The output of `board` and `board --urls` for any record is byte for byte the output on `main`, except for the change in R3.
The test pins the clock and the time zone (R16), so two runs give the same ages and clock text.
AC: Every existing `board` assertion in `test-crew-orch.sh` passes with no edit, except the assertions R3 names. One extra check seeds a record whose every time is more than a day old (each age in days, each reset a weekday), runs `board` and `board --urls` from this branch and from the `main` commit (`git show <main>:skills/orchestrator/scripts/crew-orch.py` into a temporary file), and finds the two outputs equal except the lines R3 changes. A search of `crew-orch.py` finds each derived value (the age, the marks, the status word, the row text, the merge counts, the Plan percent, the meter and the clock text) computed in one place only.

**R3. A single item's row shows its own ticket.**
The row of a single item (an item that is in no open group) shows its own ticket. The ticket is the item ticket id, linked to the ticket URL in the same way as a group ticket (an OSC 8 link on a terminal; plain text otherwise). The ticket cell follows the PR cell, with two spaces between them. A single item with no ticket shows an empty cell. The row of a grouped item shows no ticket, because the group heading shows it. The width of the ticket cell is the width of the widest ticket id among the single items. The Single items section has the ticket cell only when at least one single item has a ticket. Every row of a group is byte for byte the row on `main`. `--urls` lists the ticket of each single item in its `Links` list, in the order that the rows show them. The text "The board shows a group's ticket only" in `orchestrator-record.md` changes with this requirement. The assertion in `test-crew-orch.sh` that an item ticket is absent from `Links` changes with it.
AC: In a seeded record with one grouped item that has a ticket and one single item that has a ticket, `board` prints the single item's ticket id in its row and prints no ticket id in the grouped item's row. `board --urls` lists the single item's ticket and its URL in `Links`, and does not list the grouped item's ticket. The grouped rows equal the `main` output byte for byte. A search of `orchestrator-record.md` finds no sentence that says only a group's ticket shows on the board.

**R4. The shape is documented, with a version.**
The section "The board" of `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md` documents the JSON shape. That section stays the one owner of the board. The shape has a `version` field, an integer, which is `1` in this change. The section states the compatibility rule: a reader ignores a field it does not know; a new field does not change `version`; the removal of a field, or a change of what a field means, does. The section says that the resume part (#156) reads the same data. The description is a table of fields. It is not a dump of an example with every value.
AC: A search of the section finds a field table that names every field in "The board JSON" below, the `version` field, and the compatibility rule. The section holds no JSON example longer than 20 lines. No other file defines the shape: a search of `skills/`, `docs/`, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` for the distinctive field names `needs_you` and `launch_tab` finds them only in that section and in the code, types and tests that use them.

### The mod

**R5. The pane draws the JSON view and computes nothing.**
The mod shows the board in a pane of the orchestrator session. It gets the board only by running `python3 <plugin root>/skills/orchestrator/scripts/crew-orch.py --orch <name> board --json`, and it draws that data. The mod computes no board value: no merge value, no stage, no marks, no status word, no age, no order and no count. It does only presentation: column widths, truncation, colour, links and keys. The JSON owns the sections, every order and every cell value. The cell order of a row and the shape of a heading follow `orchestrator-record.md`'s "The board", the same as the text view. The mod may set widths, truncation, colour, links and keys, and nothing else.
AC: A test gives the mod a stub board JSON whose values differ from what the record rules would give (for example a status word `custom word` and an order that is not the merge order). The pane shows those values, in that order. A review of the mod source finds no read of `orchestrator.json` and no call to a command of `crew-orch.py` other than `board --json`.

**R6. The pane stays current with no model turn.**
The pane runs the command in R5 again on a timer, every 5 seconds while the pane is open. It does not stat or read any record file: it does not know the record path. The pane redraws when a value in the new data differs from the old data, which includes an age that changes with the clock. The pane needs no model turn to do this.
AC: A test with a fake clock and a stub command that returns data A, then data B with a changed age, finds the pane showing A, then B, after 5 seconds, with no other input. After the pane closes, the stub runs no more.

**R7. The layout follows #150.**
From the top, the pane shows:
1. The Plan section, when the board data has a `plan` that is not `null`. For each window in `plan.windows`: the label, a meter as a bar, the percent, the reset time, and the full-at forecast when the data has one. The `plan.word` shows on the 5h line, or on its own line when `plan.windows` is empty. The pane shows no meter when `plan.windows` is empty, and no Plan section when `plan` is `null`.
2. `Needs you <count>`. Each entry has the id, the kind, the age, the item and the text, oldest first. An entry with a `recommend` text has a `Recommended:` line under it.
3. One section for each open group, in the order of the data. The heading has the title, the ticket link, the repo and `<merged> of <total> merged`.
4. The `Single items` section.
5. The footer: the Done count, the key hint (`type a number and Enter to go to the tab`), and the stage legend.
The order of sections, of groups, and of rows inside a section is the order of the data. The pane does not sort.
AC: A test renders a seeded board JSON that has a Plan, two Needs-you entries (one with `recommend`), two groups and two single items. It checks the order of the sections and the rows in the rendered text. A second test renders data with `plan: null`, and the rendered text has no `Plan` line and no meter. A third test renders data with `plan.windows` empty and a `plan.word`, and the text has the word and no meter.

**R8. Links.**
The PR number is a link to the PR URL. The ticket is a link to its URL, whatever kind of URL it is (Linear, a GitHub issue or a file URL of the repo). A PR or ticket with no URL is plain text.
AC: A test renders data with a PR URL, a ticket URL, and a ticket with `url: null`. The rendered cells for the first two carry the link target. The third is plain text.

**R9. A key on a row brings the implementer's tab to the front.**
In the focused pane, the person types the row's `n` and presses Enter. That runs `python3 <plugin root>/skills/orchestrator/scripts/launcher.py focus <launch.tab>`, where the handle is the `launch_tab` of the row. A row with no handle runs nothing, and the pane shows one line that says the row has no tab. `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md` owns the command. The mod restates no exit code of it beyond what the pane shows. The pane shows a non-zero exit of the command as one line with the exit code.
AC: A test stubs the launcher. Typing `3` and Enter, where row 3 has handle `H`, runs the stub with the arguments `focus H` and no others. Typing a number of a row with `launch_tab: null` and Enter runs the stub zero times, and the pane shows the no-tab line. Typing `12` and Enter selects row 12, not row 1. A number that no row has runs nothing and shows one line.

**R10. A new Needs-you entry shows a toast once.**
The pane shows one toast for an entry id that it has not seen before in the session. The first read after the pane opens shows no toast for an entry that is already there. A reload of the mod does not toast again for an id that it already toasted. The mod keeps the seen ids in the mod API's own state (`$.state` or `$.store`), never in a file.
AC: A test reads data with entries `d1`, `q2` and checks that no toast shows. The next read adds `q3`, and exactly one toast shows, for `q3`. A third read of the same data shows no toast. After a reload of the mod, a read of the same data shows no toast.

**R11. A narrow terminal.**
At a narrow width, the pane stays usable. Every row keeps its `n`, its id, its status word and its PR, each on one line. The row text and the long fields truncate first. The mod defines the breakpoint or breakpoints, and the tests name them.
AC: A test renders the seeded data at width 40 and at width 60 (or at the widths the mod defines). Each row is one line. Each row still contains its `n`, id, status word and PR number. The row text is the part that is shortened.

**R12. The pane never writes.**
The pane never writes the orchestrator record, and it never writes any file. Its only kept state is the mod API's `$.state` or `$.store`.
AC: A test runs the pane with a stub command and a spy on file writes. The spy finds no write to a path under the record root or to `orchestrator.json`. A review of the mod source finds no write call to a file.

**R13. How the pane opens.**
The mod registers one slash command, named `orch-board`, that opens the pane. The command takes the orchestrator name as its argument. With no argument, it uses `$CREW_ORCH`. With neither, the pane shows one line that says the name is missing, and runs no command. The mod names the command in its registration, and the same name is in the README. The skill `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md` (issue #154) says when to open it. This change does not create or edit that file. The project lead reports the lines for it to the principal.
AC: A test starts the pane with an argument `x`, and the stub command receives `--orch x`. A test with no argument and `CREW_ORCH=y` receives `--orch y`. A test with neither runs the stub zero times and shows the missing-name line. `git diff main --stat` shows no change to `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md`.

### Tests, manifests and docs

**R14. Tests.**
`test-crew-orch.sh` covers `board --json`: the shape, the values, the equality with the text view for a seeded record (the same sections, the same rows in the same order, and the same `n`, id, marks, status word, PR, ticket, text and age in each row), and a single item's ticket. The mod has a test file under `tests/`, run by `claude plugin test`, as the removed review-board mod had (`git show 2b7e2e2^:tests/review-board.test.tsx`). The mod tests cover every requirement above that a test can reach: Plan present and absent, the sections and the order as the JSON gives them, links, the command of the focus key, the toast once, the narrow layout and no write. The tests stub the launcher and the board command.
AC: `bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh` exits 0. `claude plugin test` on this checkout exits 0 with every mod test passed, run as Global constraints says. `claude plugin validate` on this checkout reports no error. The mod test file has at least one test that names each of R5 to R13 that a test can reach. A checklist line in the PR body lists each of R5 to R13 that has no test, with the reason.

**R15. Manifests and docs.**
The change does these things in the same PR:
- `hooks/hooks.json` lists the mod in `modules`, beside the existing `hooks`.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` has a `types` entry if the mod uses a types file.
- `version` in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is the placeholder `0.1.TBD` in both. The PR body says so.
- `CLAUDE.md` has the mod in its Layout table and its Build state. The Build state says the mod is built and which parts a run has exercised, and no more.
- `README.md` has the new slash command, in the section that `.claude/rules/readme.md` names for a new command, with no citation.
- `docs/design.md` §15 has one new finding, numbered `§15.TBD`.
AC: A diff of the two manifests shows the same `version`, `0.1.TBD`. `jq '.modules' hooks/hooks.json` names the mod file, and `jq '.hooks | keys' hooks/hooks.json` still names `SessionEnd` and `PreCompact`. `jq '.types' .claude-plugin/plugin.json` names the types file when the mod has one. `CLAUDE.md`'s Layout table has a row for the mod, its types file and its tests. `grep -n 'TBD' docs/design.md` finds `§15.TBD`. A search of `README.md` finds the slash command, and finds no `§`.

**R16. The pane and the text view show the same board for one seeded record.**
`crew-orch.py` reads the current time from one place. A test can pin it with the environment variable `CREW_ORCH_NOW` (epoch seconds), and the test sets `TZ` too. `orchestrator-record.md` names the variable as test-only. The variable changes only the time that `board` reads. Every write still stamps the real time. `test-crew-orch.sh` seeds one record that has every kind of row: a Plan with figures (from a stub `crew-usage.py`), Needs-you entries with and without `recommend`, a group with a merged item and open items, single items with and without a ticket, and a row with no PR. first.rationale: The code renders any non-null URL as a Link with no scheme check, so the claim is literally true. But spec R8 requires links for "whatever kind of URL it is (Linear, a GitHub issue or a file URL of the repo)", so the suggested http/https-only fix would break the stated design. The URLs come from the user's own local orchestrator record, and the person must click the link.

escalated.rationale: The claim holds: the pane links any non-empty URL and never checks its scheme. But the spec (R8) asks for links to file URLs of the repo too, and the URLs come from the orchestrator's own local record, which the text view already turns into OSC 8 links. An http-only filter would break the intended design, and the security risk is small.

finding.suggested_fix: Make a missing ref fail unless an explicit opt-out variable is set.
finding.explanation: In a shallow clone, a regression in the text view would pass without a failure.
